stem: In 1708 Guru Gobind Singh passed the guruship to the Granth, declaring that there would be no human Guru after him. Where did this happen?
options: Nanded, by the Godavari river
Anandpur, in the Shivalik hills
Talwandi Sabo, in southern Punjab
Patna, by the Ganges in Bihar
why: At Nanded in the Deccan, in October 1708, Guru Gobind Singh bowed before the Granth and named it the Guru (Gurta Gaddi). Takht Sri Hazur Sahib stands there today.
source: Conferral of guruship on the Granth at Nanded, 1708 (Sikh history; Takht Sri Hazur Sahib)

es.stem: En 1708, Guru Gobind Singh entregó la guía de Gurú al Granth y declaró que después de él no habría un Gurú humano. ¿Dónde ocurrió?
options: Nanded, junto al río Godavari
Anandpur, en los montes Shivalik
Talwandi Sabo, en el sur del Punyab
Patna, junto al Ganges, en Bihar
es.why: En Nanded, en el Decán, en octubre de 1708, Guru Gobind Singh se inclinó ante el Granth y lo nombró Gurú (Gurta Gaddi). Hoy se alza allí el Takht Sri Hazur Sahib.

stem: The opening stanza of the Ardas names the Gurus one by one. What does it say comes to the one who remembers Guru Tegh Bahadur?
options: pain departs at the very sight of him
the nine treasures come running home
every enemy turns and flees the door
the eighteen powers settle in the house
why: The Ardas says "tegh bahaadar simariai, ghar nau nidh aavai dhaai": remember Tegh Bahadur and the nine treasures (nau nidh) come running home. "Seeing whom all pain goes" is said of Guru Har Krishan.
source: Ardas, opening stanza, as set out in the Sikh Rehat Maryada

es.stem: La primera estrofa del Ardas nombra a los Gurús uno por uno. ¿Qué dice que llega a quien recuerda a Guru Tegh Bahadur?
options: el dolor se va con solo verlo a él
los nueve tesoros llegan corriendo a casa
todo enemigo da la vuelta y huye
los dieciocho poderes se quedan en casa
es.why: El Ardas dice "tegh bahaadar simariai, ghar nau nidh aavai dhaai": recuerda a Tegh Bahadur y los nueve tesoros (nau nidh) llegan corriendo a casa. "Al verlo, todo dolor se va" se dice de Guru Har Krishan.

stem: The Ardas remembers the "chaalee mukte", the forty liberated ones. Who were they?
options: the first forty Sikhs given amrit at Anandpur in 1699
scribes who copied the Adi Granth for distant sangats
Sikhs who left the Guru, came back, fell at Muktsar
Sikhs who dug the sacred pool at Amritsar for Ram Das
why: Forty Sikhs deserted Guru Gobind Singh during the siege of Anandpur, returned with Mai Bhago, and died fighting at Khidrana (1705). The Guru tore up their letter of disowning and blessed them as liberated; the place became Muktsar.
source: Ardas (Sikh Rehat Maryada); battle of Khidrana/Muktsar, 1705

es.stem: El Ardas recuerda a los "chaalee mukte", los cuarenta liberados. ¿Quiénes fueron?
options: los primeros cuarenta sijs que recibieron amrit en 1699
escribas que copiaron el Adi Granth para sangats lejanas
sijs que dejaron al Gurú, volvieron, cayeron en Muktsar
sijs que cavaron el estanque sagrado de Amritsar
es.why: Cuarenta sijs abandonaron a Guru Gobind Singh durante el sitio de Anandpur, regresaron con Mai Bhago y murieron luchando en Khidrana (1705). El Gurú rompió la carta en que lo desconocían y los bendijo como liberados; el lugar pasó a llamarse Muktsar.

stem: The Ardas ends "Nanak naam chardi kala, tere bhaane sarbat da bhala." What does its second half, "tere bhaane sarbat da bhala," ask for?
options: victory for the Khalsa over all its foes
pardon for any slip made in the prayer
the good of all, within God's will
rising spirits for the Sikh sangat alone
why: Tere bhaane means "in Your will", sarbat "all", bhala "good, well-being": in Your will, may all be well. The prayer for forgiveness of slips (bhul chuk) comes just before it.
source: Ardas, closing line, as set out in the Sikh Rehat Maryada

es.stem: El Ardas termina "Nanak naam chardi kala, tere bhaane sarbat da bhala". ¿Qué pide su segunda mitad, "tere bhaane sarbat da bhala"?
options: la victoria del Khalsa sobre sus enemigos
perdón por cualquier error en la oración
el bien de todos, en la voluntad de Dios
ánimo en alto solo para la sangat sij
es.why: Tere bhaane significa "en Tu voluntad", sarbat "todos", bhala "el bien, el bienestar": en Tu voluntad, que todos estén bien. La petición de perdón por los errores (bhul chuk) viene justo antes.

stem: In Guru Ram Das's laavan (Raag Suhi, Ang 773–774), the four stanzas sung at the Anand Karaj, what does the fourth round describe?
options: the call to live a householder's life of dharma
the mind freed of fear by meeting the true Guru
a deep longing for the Lord rising in the heart
the mind at ease in sahaj, one with the Lord
why: The fourth lav says the mind becomes calm and the Lord is found in sahaj, natural ease. Round one sets out dharma, round two fearlessness and the washing away of ego, round three longing (bairaag).
source: Guru Granth Sahib, Suhi Mahalla 4, Chhant (laavan), Ang 773–774

es.stem: En las laavan de Guru Ram Das (Raag Suhi, Ang 773–774), las cuatro estrofas que se cantan en el Anand Karaj, ¿qué describe la cuarta vuelta?
options: el llamado a vivir el dharma como jefe de hogar
la mente libre de miedo al encontrar al Gurú verdadero
un hondo anhelo del Señor que crece en el corazón
la mente en calma en sahaj, unida al Señor
es.why: La cuarta lav dice que la mente se calma y se encuentra al Señor en sahaj, la calma natural. La primera vuelta habla del dharma, la segunda de no tener miedo y de lavar el ego, la tercera del anhelo (bairaag).

stem: A Sikh family is about to open a new shop and wants to follow the Sikh Rehat Maryada. What does the Rehat Maryada say is offered before beginning any task?
options: the Laavan, the four rounds
an Ardas, the standing prayer
the Sohila, the night prayer
the Mool Mantar, said five times
why: The Sikh Rehat Maryada's section on Ardas says an Ardas should be offered before undertaking any task. The Ardas itself asks that everyone's tasks be brought to a good end (sarbat de kaaraj raas karne).
source: Sikh Rehat Maryada, section on Ardas

es.stem: Una familia sij está por abrir una tienda nueva y quiere seguir el Sikh Rehat Maryada. ¿Qué dice el Rehat Maryada que se ofrece antes de empezar cualquier tarea?
options: las Laavan, las cuatro vueltas
un Ardas, la oración de pie
el Sohila, la oración de la noche
el Mool Mantar, dicho cinco veces
es.why: La sección sobre el Ardas del Sikh Rehat Maryada dice que se debe ofrecer un Ardas antes de emprender cualquier tarea. El propio Ardas pide que las tareas de todos lleguen a buen fin (sarbat de kaaraj raas karne).

stem: In Guru Nanak's shabad in Sri Rag (Guru Granth Sahib, Ang 14) that begins with a palace of pearls and jewels, what is the hymn saying about wealth and power?
why: Sri Rag M1, Ang 14 (moti ta mandar oosareh): a palace of pearls, a floor of jewels, a siddha's powers, a sultan's throne; each time the Guru asks that, seeing these, he not forget the Lord, for without the Name the soul burns.
source: Guru Granth Sahib, Sri Rag Mahalla 1, Ang 14

rubric.point: says the danger is that riches, pleasures or power make a person forget God or the Name; the hymn asks not to forget. saying only "wealth is evil" or "give up all wealth" does not count.
says that without God or the Name all of it is worth nothing (the soul burns, there is no other place). "money doesn't buy happiness" with no link to God is partly met.
mentions the hymn's rising images (palace, jeweled floor or companion, miraculous powers, a sultan's throne) or the refrain (rahao).

es.stem: En el shabad de Guru Nanak en Sri Rag (Guru Granth Sahib, Ang 14) que empieza con un palacio de perlas y joyas, ¿qué dice el himno sobre la riqueza y el poder?
es.why: Sri Rag M1, Ang 14 (moti ta mandar oosareh): un palacio de perlas, un piso de joyas, los poderes de un siddha, el trono de un sultán; cada vez el Gurú pide que, al ver todo eso, no olvide al Señor, porque sin el Nombre el alma arde.

stem: In Guru Nanak's hymn addressed to Bhai Lalo in Raag Tilang (Guru Granth Sahib, Ang 722–723), what does he describe, and on what authority does he say he speaks?
why: Tilang M1, Ang 722–723 (jaisee mai aavai khasam kee baanee): Guru Nanak tells Lalo of Babur's invasion, the violence and the suffering of women of every community, and says he speaks as the Master's word comes to him.
source: Guru Granth Sahib, Tilang Mahalla 1, Ang 722–723

rubric.point: says it describes Babur's invasion of Punjab (the sack of Saidpur) and its violence and suffering. a general "a war" with no invader or suffering named is partly met.
says he speaks as the Lord's or Master's word (bani) comes to him, not from his own opinion.
mentions any detail: Lalo was a carpenter and friend of Guru Nanak; the invader came "like a wedding party of sin"; qazis and brahmins were pushed aside; women of every community suffered.

es.stem: En el himno de Guru Nanak dirigido a Bhai Lalo en Raag Tilang (Guru Granth Sahib, Ang 722–723), ¿qué describe, y con qué autoridad dice que habla?
es.why: Tilang M1, Ang 722–723 (jaisee mai aavai khasam kee baanee): Guru Nanak le cuenta a Lalo la invasión de Babur, la violencia y el sufrimiento de las mujeres de todas las comunidades, y dice que habla según le llega la palabra del Señor.
